payload.summary: Ward Flow: the Command prototype and the shipped reducer disagree about whether a prior decline is final
payload.detail: VERIFIED 2026-09-09. The third-edition Command mockup (docs/ward-flow/mockups/command-third-edition.html) lists prior_decline in ABSOLUTE_GATES and prints the fixed sentence 'A recorded reason does not undo a ward's decline', so a coordinator taught by the prototype learns that a ward which has declined is closed to that patient. The shipped reducer (src/components/ward-management/ward-flow-reducer.ts, the comment block above SUITABILITY_GATES, around lines 441 to 452) deliberately leaves prior_decline out of both the world-fact group and SUITABILITY_GATES: a ward that declined ninety minutes ago because it had no bed is the commonest thing in bed management, beds free up, none of the five OVERRIDE_REASONS names a mismatch that exists, and enforcing it broke 23 tests across 7 files. The comment records the question as open for the owner. So the prototype teaches one rule and the engine runs another. NEXT ACTION: the owner decides whether re-approaching a ward that declined needs a recorded reason (engine changes, tests re-proved) or is routine (the mockup's gate moves out of ABSOLUTE_GATES and its sentence goes); then write the decision into section 8.4 of docs/ward-flow/mockups/WARD-FLOW-DESIGN-SYSTEM.md so the next mockup inherits it. HARD GATE BEFORE ANY REAL-PATIENT USE, because the two accounts differ about what the coordinator may do next.
payload.source: Ward Flow design review, 2026-09-09: the reviewing Codex chat's findings F1 to F4, each re-verified against the code by the design-review chat; the owner approved recording them the same day
